title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing
authors: Dayu Li, Naibin Zhou, Zhiyuan Chen, Zihua Chen, Yu Xu, Yuan Li, Daojin Fan, Wenhao Chu, Xiawei Chen, Hui Deng, Jiacheng Gui, Linyin Hong, Bo Fan, Weiping Lin, Haonan Zou, Haoxin Lou, Xintao Zhao, Sirui Cao, Ying Chong, Qingling Zhu, Chen Wang, Yisen Hu, Kaili Zhang, Feifan Su, Haibin Zhang, Jianghan Yin, Yajie Du, Yinan Jiang, Haoping Luo, Weifeng Yang, Jiafei Wang, Jin Lin, Futian Liang, Hao Rong, Kai Yan, Ming Gong, Jinjin Li, Maliang Liu, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Shaowei Li, Xiaobo Zhu, Jian-Wei Pan
abstract: Universal fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computers are expected to require millions of physical qubits; yet extending the prevailing dedicated-control-line paradigm to this scale would exceed the wiring density and cooling-power budget of dilution refrigerators. Microwave frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) revolutionized classical communications by enabling many independent channels to share common transmission infrastructure. Translating this principle to superconducting quantum control, however, requires an all-microwave architecture and experimental validation of frequency-multiplexed gate control. Recent work in quantum error correction has demonstrated microwave-based readout, single-qubit gates and leakage suppression, whereas two-qubit gates remain predominantly driven by unipolar pulses and thus constitute the missing element of an all-microwave architecture. Here, we propose a periodically extensible hybrid multiplexing framework in which all gate operations are frequency-division multiplexed using polychromatic microwave pulses and band-pass filters, thereby reducing the required control-line count by one to two orders of magnitude. In a 1:4 demonstration, we achieve average errors of $(6.4\pm0.2)\times10^{-3}$ for parallel FDM CZ gates and $(10.6\pm0.2)\times10^{-4}$ for parallel FDM $XY(π/2)$ gates, without statistically significant multiplexing-induced degradation. Together with on-chip DC sources, this FDM-based gate-control scheme completes the last missing module in a scalable multiplexed-control architecture toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing.
summary: This paper introduces a Frequency-Division Multiplexing (FDM) framework to overcome the physical wiring limitations of scaling superconducting quantum computers. By encoding multiple gate operations onto shared, frequency-multiplexed microwave pulses, the required control-line count is drastically reduced. The work experimentally validates this approach, showing high-fidelity gate operations in a multiplexed environment.
main_problem: Scaling fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computers faces severe limitations due to the wiring density and cooling-power budget when using dedicated control lines for millions of qubits.
main_result: The proposed Frequency-Division Multiplexing (FDM) framework successfully demonstrates gate operations while maintaining low error rates, significantly reducing the required control-line count by orders of magnitude.
method: The authors propose a hybrid multiplexing framework where all gate operations are encoded onto polychromatic microwave pulses and spectrally routed using band-pass filters.
model_or_system: The system is based on superconducting transmon qubits coupled via tunable couplers, analyzed using a three-mode QCQ model. The control mechanism leverages frequency-division multiplexing to share a common control bus.
key_observables: Average gate errors for parallel FDM CZ and XY gates, sequence fidelity (XEB, SPB, Leakage), and the thermal load on the mixing-chamber.
important_parameters: Multiplexing ratios (e.g., 1:4 demonstration), required control-line reduction (up to 1/48), and the frequency separation ($\Delta$) between multiplexed channels.
main_assumptions: The scheme assumes the feasibility of an all-microwave architecture for two-qubit gates and relies on the effectiveness of band-pass filtering and waveform pre-distortion to mitigate crosstalk.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scalable control architecture, the thermal load reduction vs. multiplexing ratio, and the spectral components of the microwave pulses used for gate control.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the scaling bottleneck, then proposes the FDM multiplexing framework, details the gate implementation (MP-CZ gates), provides simulation results showing error rates, and concludes by demonstrating the feasibility of the scalable control scheme.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering bottleneck of scaling superconducting quantum processors by proposing a fundamental architectural shift in control electronics, which is crucial for realizing large-scale quantum computation.
